methods.latency: Eight alternating pairs of published release budget tests, plus actual Msg::Meters and Msg::TimeChanged offscreen fixtures (100 warmups, 1000 measured events per run, scale 2). Percentiles use sorted samples at floor(n*p); aggregate percentiles are medians of per-run percentiles. Background builds/VMs were active on November 6.
methods.watcher: Two runs of 60 atomic saves per revision at deterministic randomized 1..999 ms intervals. Latency from rename start to callback entry, production 1 s fallback interval.
methods.window: Published window-cost.py: ten paired runs, 3 s settle, 15 s idle. Forty-pair startup follow-up shortened post-map settle to 0.1 s and idle to 0.05 s; only startup fields from the follow-up are used.
methods.native_idle: Background jobs stopped. Published session-idle.py with 30 s settle, 60 s idle, three alternating pairs per resolution. Power from RAPL boundary reads via the existing 1 Hz service; counter timestamps and wrap range determine watts. No extra 100 Hz sampling loop. Desktop applications remain active.
methods.energy: Six alternating pairs of 100000 meter updates plus 100 warmups, the same release fixture binaries. PPT sampled every 10 ms. Above-background joules = batch joules - duration * mean(pre-baseline watts, post-baseline watts); both baselines last 15 s.
methods.scope: Headless/offscreen component measurements. Power covers CPU cores, integrated GPU and IO die, excluding DRAM, NVIDIA GPU, display and PSU. No physical-display latency or battery-life measurement.
methods.data: results.json retains every measured run and all integrated power readings/counter boundaries. latency-samples.json.gz retains the 1000-event fixture samples. power-samples.tsv.gz retains all fixed-work PPT traces; the 100000 individual event timings per energy run are summarized by sum/percentiles/max. Temporary binary paths are relative to the before/after snapshots.
